name: Tortus AI
description: Tortus AI is a UK-focused clinical AI scribe designed specifically for NHS workflows and UK EHR systems like EMIS Web, SystmOne, and Vision. Pricing starts at £44/month for pilot licenses (up to 20 users), with enterprise deployments at £200K/year for NHS Trusts (up to 100,000 audio hours). Tortus is procurable through NHS-compliant routes including Crown Commercial Service and NHS Technology Services 3. Key differentiator: purpose-built for NHS administrative burden—outpatient, ED, and primary care documentation with UK clinical workflows. Partnership tiers offer revenue-share against productivity outcomes. Not for US practices (no HIPAA focus) or non-UK healthcare systems.

faqs.q: How much does Tortus AI cost for NHS practices?
faqs.a: Tortus offers pilot licenses at £44/month per user (up to 20 users, 1-year max), 3-month pilots at £15,000 for up to 100 users, and enterprise deployments at £200,000/year for NHS Trusts (up to 100,000 audio hours, then £2/hour). Partnership tiers with revenue-share are also available.

faqs.q: Is Tortus available through NHS procurement routes?
faqs.a: Yes. Tortus is procurable through Crown Commercial Service (direct award, no further competition required) and NHS Technology Services 3 Dynamic Purchasing System for trusts preferring a mini-competition route.

faqs.q: What UK EHRs does Tortus integrate with?
faqs.a: Tortus integrates natively with EMIS Web (UK's most widely used GP system), SystmOne, and Vision—covering the majority of UK primary care and hospital clinical systems.

faqs.q: Is Tortus AI HIPAA compliant for US practices?
faqs.a: No. Tortus is designed specifically for UK NHS workflows with GDPR compliance and UK data residency. US practices should use Freed ($39-119/mo), Commure Scribe ($59-89/mo), or other HIPAA-focused alternatives.

faqs.q: Tortus vs Heidi Health for UK GPs: which is better?
faqs.a: Tortus is purpose-built for NHS workflows with native EMIS/SystmOne integration and NHS-compliant procurement routes. Heidi Health is more international. For UK GPs, Tortus offers tighter NHS alignment; for global practices or those wanting cross-border flexibility, Heidi may be more suitable.
